#2660. Castle, Spurs rout Warriors for 11th straight win

Planes were grounded nationwide on Friday night and the San Antonio Spurs grounded the Golden State Warriors from the opening tip in their second NBA Cup game. Fueled by Stephon Castle, the Spurs took a 20-point first quarter lead and never looked back as they defeated the Warriors 123-85 at the Frost Bank Center.

The victory is the 11th straight for San Antonio, who also improved to 2-0 in NBA Cup play and control their own destiny to advance to the knockout stage of the competition. The Spurs would need only one win in their next two Cup games to book a spot in the next round.

Nothing the Stephen Curry-less Warriors tried on Friday worked against the Spurs, who led by as many as 43 points in the game. Stephon Castle rebounded from a few poor outings in the last few games to score a season-high 32 points to go along with six assists and five rebounds. Castle shot 12-of-18 from the field as he scored 13 of the Spurs' first 26 points.

"He's in the middle of everything," Coach Johnson said of Castle. "He's an unbelievable impact player. He's never blinked at anything we've asked. He's never shown any poor body language. He just attacks everything. And there are times in this league, that is ridiculously difficult."

Early on, it was obvious what type of night this was going to be for the Spurs. San Antonio scored the first 18 points of the game and did not allow Golden State to score their first points until there was 5:54 left in the opening period. The Spurs' defense was swarming all through the first quarter, getting hands into the passing lanes and by the time the buzzer sounded to end the period, the Warriors only had 14 points were shooting 21 percent.

"I think the defense probably ignites the offense more than vice versa," Johnson said. "So I still lean into the defense. Thought we were pretty on point with some of our game plan execution stuff and attention to detail."

Golden State's standout rookie Yaxel Lendeborg struggled, shooting just 1-for-13 and ended with the game just three points. Credit to Victor Wembanyama and Luke Kornet, who both worked to make life difficult for the rookie.

"Nobody wanted to go into the paint," Lendeborg said. "Nobody wanted to get their shot blocked by him. So we were all just doing some weak-ass floaters. I don't know how many of us work on those.

San Antonio won all four quarters, but a 34-27 third quarter forced Coach Johnson to sit the starters and put his bench in with the Spurs comfortably ahead by 37 points. The majority of the fourth quarter saw Tarris Reed Jr., Carter Bryant, Jordan McLaughlin, and Keldon Johnson take the floor in mop up duty.

The win also saw the return of Devin Vassell, who missed the previous two games with adductor tightness. De'Aaron Fox was questionable with soreness, but he also took the floor in the win for the Spurs.

Victor Wembanyama had a quiet 12 points and 12 rebounds, but he was also hit in the throat, poked in the eye, and thrown to the floor by Draymond Green. After the game, Wemby commented on this and said he was "not surprised" by Green's flagrant foul.

De'Aaron Fox did not have his shot on Friday, going just 1-of-7 from the floor. However, he made up for that by doing the little things. He had five rebounds, four assists to contribute in a different way.

Keldon Johnson is starting to look like the man who won Sixth Man of the Year last season. He scored 18 points off the bench to go along with four rebounds and four assists in 25 minutes. If he can do that consistently, it makes the Spurs even more dangerous than they already are.

The Spurs (11-2) will now hit the road to face the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center for the final time this season on Sunday afternoon at 4 p.m. central time.

#2659. 'How does that happen?': Nick Saban dismisses College Football Playoff rankings

Nick Saban has openly opposed the newly legitimized expanded 24-team College Football Playoff on more than one occasion, and he isn't particularly fond of the College Football Playoff rankings, either.

On Friday's Pat McAfee Show, the legendary Alabama head football coach let it rip when Pat McAfee asked him to weigh in on this week's rankings.

"To be honest with you, I think, at this point, the rankings are a little bit bullsh*t, if you want to know the truth about it," Saban said. "I think there's so many games to play and so many scenarios and all that. Who wins what is going to determine—like, UCLA being No. 4 doesn't mean nothing if they can win out and beat USC. USC being 20th doesn't mean anything if they beat Indiana and go beat UCLA."

"As you see people move up and down based on wins and losses—I mean, Indiana didn't even play, and they dropped, what? Five spots or something," Saban added. "I'm like, how does that happen? But it happens. If they win this week, they'll be right back in the mix of things."

Saban is far from the first or last person to disparage the College Football Playoff rankings.

Upon the season's first ranking releasing on Nov. 3, the College Football Playoff selection committee was universally bemoaned opinion across sports media. According to Rece Davis, who hosts ESPN's rankings show, the committee indulged in "some course correction" with this week's rankings.

Ultimately, as Saban said, objective game results matter more than subjective rankings—or at least they should. Check out this weekend's consequential slate here.

#2658. Rams vs. Arizona Cardinals: How to watch, start time, odds and prediction

Myles Garrett is coming off a dominating three-sack performance in his return to the Rams' lineup.

"Not a 100 [%]," he told reporters Friday when asked to put a percentage-gauge on how he felt in last Sunday's victory over the Washington Commanders. "I can't go that far. We're not a 100 but we're trying to make our way there."

Garrett, who sat out seven games while recovering from left knee surgery, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals. But he is expected to play as the Rams attempt to extend their winning streak to four games.

The two-time NFL defensive player of the year's influence on the team extends beyond the field.

In the locker room, the 10th-year pro is the top-rated player in a player-organized, no-contact shadow-boxing league designed to instill competition and camaraderie.

Garrett, who spent his first nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns, said he didn't bring the competition with him, "but I will say I was the top dog where I left and top dog now, so not much has changed."

Garrett said he does not back down from a challenge by teammates.

Coach Sean McVay welcomes the team-building component of the competition.

"It's always about when can you find those times to lock in but when can you do those things that organically occur to create a camaraderie and a connection that is something that only the players can really be able to do," McVay said. "When you're hearing laughs, I think that's the sign of a good culture."

Garrett played 37 of 62 defensive snaps against the Commanders and said he was "tired as hell" afterward.

After the Rams play the Cardinals, they will have what will essentially be a mini-bye before playing the Green Bay Packers on the night before Thanksgiving.

Garrett said the bye was coming at "a perfect time" for all players.

"Being able to get some extra practice myself, being on the field and being able to train and work on some things, get in my rhythm even without some games, I think will help us all in the long run," he said.

Rams: OL Steve Avila (hamstring, out); TE Terrance Ferguson (hamstring, out); Myles Garrett (knee, questionable), CB Trent McDuffie (back, questionable); S Kam Curl (toe, questionable); TE Davis Allen (oblique, questionable); LS Joe Cardona (ankle, questionable).

Cardinals: DL Zach Carter (knee, out); OL Hjalte Froholdt (concussion, out); OL Jon Gaines II (ankle, out); TE Hunter Long (knee, questionable); CB Max Melton (knee/hand, questionable); OL Jayden Williams (knee, questionable); S Andrew Wingard (groin, questionable).

The Rams and the Cardinals will play Sunday at 1:05 p.m. PST at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz. The game will be shown in Southern California on CBS and Paramount+. #2657. Lazio-Inter, Supercoppa a San Siro: sei cambi possibili nei supplementari

Il regolamento consente fino a cinque sostituzioni nei tempi regolamentari; la sfida è fissata al 22 dicembre alle 21:00.

Inter e Lazio si affronteranno martedì 22 dicembre 2026 alle 21:00 a San Siro per la Supercoppa italiana. La trentanovesima edizione, denominata ufficialmente EA SPORTS FC Supercup, si giocherà in gara unica. La Lega Calcio Serie A ha ufficializzato data, orario, sede e regolamento della partita con un comunicato.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La sfida al Meazza prevede due tempi supplementari da 15 minuti ciascuno se il risultato sarà in parità dopo i 90 minuti regolamentari. Se la parità dovesse persistere, la Supercoppa verrà assegnata ai calci di rigore.

Per la loro esecuzione si applicheranno le modalità indicate nel «Regolamento del Giuoco del Calcio», al paragrafo «Procedure per determinare la squadra vincente di una gara». Inter-Lazio sarà trasmessa in diretta sulle reti Mediaset.

Ciascuna squadra potrà effettuare fino a cinque sostituzioni, utilizzando non più di tre interruzioni di gioco, oltre all’intervallo tra i due tempi. Se si andrà ai supplementari, sarà disponibile una quarta interruzione. Restano inoltre utilizzabili le pause tra la fine dei tempi regolamentari e l’inizio del primo supplementare, e tra il primo e il secondo supplementare.

Solo in caso di tempi supplementari sarà consentito un ulteriore cambio: il limite delle sostituzioni salirà così a sei per squadra.

Il comunicato della Lega disciplina anche le squalifiche di calciatori e tecnici. Chi è in diffida e riceve un’ammonizione nella giornata di campionato precedente la Supercoppa sconterà la squalifica nella successiva gara di campionato. La stessa collocazione è prevista per la squalifica, o per la parte residua della sanzione, di chi viene espulso nella giornata precedente la Supercoppa o ha già una sanzione da scontare; se necessario, il provvedimento riguarderà più gare di campionato.

Anche un calciatore o tecnico già in diffida che venga ammonito durante la Supercoppa sconterà la squalifica nella successiva partita di campionato. Per un’espulsione nella gara del 22 dicembre, la squalifica sarà invece scontata nella gara o nelle gare di campionato successive.

#2655. San Antonio wastes no time blowing out the Warriors

There are good starts… and then there are very good starts. An 18-0 run to begin the game against one of the best offenses in the league qualifies as an outstanding start. The San Antonio Spurs built a 38-14 first-quarter lead over the Golden State Warriors on their way to a 123-85 win.

The Spurs were led in large part by the stellar offensive play of Stephon Castle. The guard is coming off a stretch of bad play, but turned it around in a major way against the Warriors. Castle had 32 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds. He had it going from deep, hitting a trio of three-pointers in the first quarter, and finished the game shooting 5-for-7 from three.

Castle did more than just hit open threes. The Warriors had no answer for his physical, downhill brand of basketball. With Draymond Green attached at Victor Wembanyama's hip, Castle and the Spurs guards got to the basket with little to no resistance at the rim. San Antonio outscored Golden State 56-to-28 in the paint.

Castle's passing was on point against the Warriors. He had no turnovers despite having the ball in his hands for a lot of the game. He was particularly effective on the primary and secondary fast breaks, where Golden State was slow to get back.

Castle and Wembanyama had the Area 51 connection working early and often. Wembanyama wasn't able to get free in the half-court too often with Green playing physical basketball, but San Antonio was able to get him a few lobs out of the pick-and-roll.

It wasn't just Wembanyama receiving lobs from Castle; he also delivered them. Sometimes it's easy to take this stuff for granted because of all the amazing things that Wembanyama can do… but this is your 7-foot-5 center dribbling the ball up and throwing an underhand lob to his point guard for a reverse slam. That is versatility in one play! Wembanyama ended the game with 12 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists, and 2 blocks.

To further add insult to injury, the duo did it again just a few minutes later!

Early in the game, the Spurs ran a lot of pick-and-rolls with Wembanyama handling the ball, and their guards setting picks. The Warriors sent doubles at Wembanyama on these plays, making it easy for the guards to slip into the paint and create easy looks. Here, Dylan Harper is able to get to the basket and finish over Golden State's smaller defenders.

Golden State left the paint essentially wide open all game long. It felt like the Spurs could touch the lane whenever they wanted to. Harper carved up the defense with his tight handle for a nifty finish in the second quarter. Harper had a quiet but efficient game, scoring 9 points on 4-of-8 shooting.

Harper also nailed a transition three on one of the most memorable plays of the night. Shortly after the ball went into the basket, Green shoulder-checked Wembanyama into the ground and received a flagrant foul.

Wembanyama finished the game with seemingly no health issues despite the hard hit. He and the rest of the Spurs will get a day off before a rematch with the Utah Jazz on Sunday as they look to win their twelfth game in a row.

#2654. Big Blue View mailbag: Kickoff rule, Rasul Douglas interception, more

Lou Catalano asks: Could you please explain the rule concerning kickoffs going out of bounds? In the Giants/Washington game, the ball bounced in bounds, the returner stepped out of bounds, then caught the ball while his knee was touching the ground in bounds. What ever happpened to the old John Madden maxim that one knee equals two feet?

Ed says: Lou, you weren't the only confused by this. The rulebook says:

"A ball that is in player possession is out of bounds when the runner is out of bounds."

On kickoffs, this is a bit of a loophole. Credit Luke McCaffrey of the Commanders for knowing the rule and making a great play. If you plant your feet out of bounds, then touch a ball that is inbounds, it makes the ball considered to be out of bounds. That creates a kickoff out of bounds and puts the ball at the 40-yard line.

I have seen this happen a couple of times. I have also seen players mess this up by either catching the ball and stepping out of bounds, or by picking the ball up inbounds right near the sideline and trying to return it.

David Silver asks: I'm trying to make sense out of the last throw JJ McCarthy made to Nabers that was intercepted. It looks like McCarthy hung the ball up based on the trajectory. It also gave Nabers plenty of time to get it sighted. Douglas comes from behind to high point Nabers, but it also looked like he hit Nabers early. But that is a 50/50 ball Nabers wants. My question is, bad throw, bad catch attempt, great defensive play, or pass interference?

Ed says: David, sometimes you just have to give the other guy credit. I have watched this play a bunch of times, and I listened to Nabers and John Harbaugh talk about it on Friday.

Washington sent a zero blitz, rushing more players than the Giants could block and forcing J.J. McCarthy to make a split-second decision. His decision was to give the Giants' best receiver a chance to make a play. Right decision? Wrong decision? Harbaugh just said it was the decision that McCarthy made. Douglas didn't interfere with Nabers. Nabers said he was focused on tracking the ball and knew there was a defender in the area, but didn't know where. Douglas did not interfere with Nabers. He just ended up making a play.

The Giants have won a couple of games like that this season. The other guys get paid, too.

Raymond Dansereau asks: How much better are the Giants really than last year? Last year they had a tough schedule and close losses; this year, they're playing a weak schedule and really not always looking great. Defense seems better, but is this a 10-7 playoffs team that gets beaten badly in the first round? Or, does this look like sustainable improvement? Or too soon to say?

Ed says: Raymond, I can't go position-by-position or player-by-player in a mailbag response. I think the real answer is that the Giants are better simply because they have John Harbaugh and they are coached better. It doesn't hurt that this team has Arvell Reese, either.

The Giants are winning close games, which they couldn't do last year. A lot of that is coaching, whether it is in-game decisions or just preparing players well enough that they believe they are supposed to make plays and win close games.

If it is a 9-7-1 playoff team that gets bounced in the first round, what's wrong with that? The Giants won seven games combined the past two seasons — a playoff berth would be a fantastic accomplishment. Sustainable improvement? The NFL is such a week-to-week and year-to-year league that is impossible to say. As long as Harbaugh is the coach, though, the Giants have a chance to be relevant. That is a massive improvement.

Matt Smith asks: We've had four failures in a row at the head coach position. They are bookended by two Hall of Fame coaches. My question is, seeing how far the gap is between Daboll and Harbaugh, do you find it surprising how long we waited to move on from him? It seems more and more apparent to me that we had talent that we could've done with if we had a professional head coach with standards. The red flags were always there.

Ed says: Matt, I'm not at all surprised that the Giants waited as long as they did to move on from Brian Daboll. look at the Giants' track record:

Ben McAdoo lasted less than two full seasons.

Joe Judge was fired (well, he kinda fired himself) after two seasons.

You cannot get ahead when you have to keep blowing things up and starting over every two years. That means an entire new coaching staff, gutting most of the roster, and starting over. You can never institute a real philosophy or build anything that way.

John Mara knew it, and he said several times that he knew he needed to be more patient than he had been.

Daboll had a shockingly good first season and won Coach of the Year. The Giants could have justified firing him and GM Joe Schoen after a 3-14 2024 season, but chose not to.

Mike Vrabel got hired by New England that offseason. Zero chance he was picking the Giants over the Patriots, the team he played for an an organization he loves. Ben Johnson got hired by the Bears. No chance he was picking the Giants over the Bears, who already had Caleb Williams in place. Liam Coen got hired by the Jaguars, but nobody knew that would work out as well as it had.

It was really the 2025 season when it became clear that the coaching staff wasn't maximizing the talent of the players.

Adam Singer asks: During the game against the Eagles, it looked like some of the players had a diagonal line through the word "GIANTS" on their helmets while others did not. What was going on there?

Ed says: Adam, the word 'GIANTS' was underlined. I think what you saw was the chinstrip, which buckles on the side of the helmet, protruding over the lettering on some of the helmets.

Ronald Lukoff asks: I usually do not disagree with a lot of your comments but I do take exception to your thoughts about the Giants making a blockbuster trade today (this is written Tuesday morning). I have been a Giant fan since 1956. I have seen a lot of success and a lot of failure. This team is made up of a lot of draft picks and I really do not want to give up future draft choices for a player that can give us a division title. This team has only played one team with a record above .500. Do you really think that one player is worth losing draft capital? If I thought one player could get us to the Super Bowl, I might feel differently. Do you think JJ is the answer at QB. He was great first 5 quarters, not so much last game. but a quarterback needy ream just traded him away, so I am hesitant to put all my faith in him and believe me, I hope I'm wrong. I feel like we are at least a year away from potentially going to the Super Bowl and while I would love to win the division, I just don't think giving up draft choices is the best way to build a championship team. You're feelings?

Ed says: Ronald, it's moot at this point since the trade deadline has come and gone. I want to clarify this, anyway.

I wrote earlier in the week that the Giants should try to capitalize on the opportunity they have in the NFC East. You don't know if or when that opportunity will come again.

They did try to do that. They were very aggressive. They were also careful. I said earlier in the week there was a price they should not go to — meaning they should not go above the second-round pick they had offered the Colts for Jonathan Taylor. They — rightly — refused to do that.

I said all along the end game is not winning the division this year and then going back to being a third- or fourth-place team for fove years after that. The end game is to be a championship contender on a consistent basis. You have to protect your future to do that.

#2652. Bears Week 10 Flashbacks: Concannon’s Bombs, Dent’s Dominance, Vasher’s 108 yards

The Bears may be enjoying their bye week, but the Gridiron Time Machine doesn't need the week off.

Instead of our usual three games, we're digging a little deeper this week with five memorable Week 10 performances, spanning nearly 60 years of Bears history.

The 1967 Bears were sitting at 4-5 when the St. Louis Cardinals came to Wrigley Field for Week 10.

What followed was one of the more explosive passing performances of the era.

Jack Concannon completed only 11 passes, but those completions went for an incredible 336 yards and three touchdowns. Dick Gordon was responsible for most of the damage, catching four passes for 179 yards and two scores.

The touchdowns were not exactly short ones either.

Concannon connected with Gordon for a 93-yard touchdown early in the second quarter, then found Bob Jones for another 51-yard score. Before halftime arrived, Gordon struck again from 67 yards out.

Three touchdown passes. All three from more than 50 yards away.

Meanwhile, the Bears defense made sure St. Louis never had much of an opportunity to respond.

Chicago intercepted Cardinals quarterbacks seven times, including five picks from Jim Hart alone, while forcing nine turnovers overall. The Cardinals finished with only 230 total yards and never reached the end zone.

Chicago cruised to a 30-3 victory behind 461 yards of offense.

For a franchise that has not exactly been known for explosive passing attacks, Concannon throwing three touchdown passes of 51 yards or longer feels almost out of place in Bears history.

The Bears entered Week 10 of the 1979 season sitting at 4-5 and desperately trying to remain in the playoff picture.

Detroit turned out to be a pretty good opponent for getting things moving in the right direction.

Walter Payton once again carried the offense, rushing for 113 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries while adding another 53 yards as a receiver. Mike Phipps threw for just 136 yards, but Chicago didn't need much through the air.

The fun really started in the third quarter.

With Chicago leading 14-7, Steve Schubert returned a punt 77 yards for a touchdown. Not long afterward, Terry Schmidt intercepted Lions quarterback Jeff Komlo and returned it 20 yards for another score.

Suddenly, a seven-point game had become a 28-7 Bears lead.

Payton added his second touchdown in the fourth quarter to finish off a 35-7 victory.

Chicago did not commit a turnover while forcing five from Detroit, and Payton finished with 166 yards from scrimmage. The win moved the Bears back to .500 at 5-5 and became part of a late-season push that eventually carried Chicago into the playoffs.

Give the ball to Walter Payton, let the defense create mistakes, and sneak in a special teams touchdown while you're at it.

One year before the 1985 Bears defense became immortal, Chicago was already showing the rest of the NFL what was coming.

The defending Super Bowl champion Los Angeles Raiders arrived at Soldier Field in Week 10 with a 7-2 record.

Walter Payton handled the offensive workload, rushing 27 times for 111 yards and scoring twice in the first half. His touchdown runs of 18 and eight yards gave Chicago a 14-0 advantage before the defense took care of everything else.

Dent recorded 4.5 sacks, which remains the Bears' single-game franchise record. Chicago sacked Raiders quarterbacks nine times overall, forced five turnovers and held Los Angeles to just 181 total yards.

The Raiders managed only two field goals in a 17-6 Bears victory. It was the first time the defending champions had been held without a touchdown in more than three years.

The win moved Chicago to 7-3 and gave the Bears another indication that Buddy Ryan's defense was developing into something special.

But before the Super Bowl Shuffle, the playoff shutouts and the legend of the 1985 defense, Richard Dent and company were already making Sundays miserable for opposing quarterbacks.

The defending Super Bowl champions just happened to get an early preview.

The Bears entered Week 10 of the 1990 season as one of the hottest teams in football.

Atlanta came to Soldier Field and nearly spoiled the afternoon.

After falling behind 3-0, Chicago scored 24 unanswered points behind touchdowns from Neal Anderson, Wendell Davis and Brad Muster. Jim Harbaugh connected with Davis for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the Bears carried a 24-3 advantage into the second half.

Atlanta scored two unanswered touchdowns to cut the lead to 24-17, and what had looked like a comfortable afternoon suddenly became a one-score game.

Fortunately, Chris Miller threw one pass too many.

Vestee Jackson jumped the route and returned the interception 45 yards for a touchdown, pushing the lead back to 30-17 with just over a minute remaining. Atlanta scored once more, but Chicago held on for a 30-24 victory.

Miller threw for 239 yards and two touchdowns, but the Bears intercepted him four times. Wendell Davis led Chicago offensively with five catches for 105 yards and a score, while Harbaugh added 195 passing yards and another 47 on the ground.

The victory improved Chicago to 8-1 and extended its winning streak to five games.

Sometimes the defense dominates from start to finish.

Other times it waits until things get interesting before reminding everyone who is in charge.

If you remember anything about the Bears' 2005 Week 10 win over San Francisco, it probably isn't the offense.

Chicago quarterback Kyle Orton threw for only 67 yards. San Francisco quarterback Cody Pickett somehow managed just one completion for 28 yards.

With gusts approaching 50 miles per hour at Soldier Field, 49ers kicker Joe Nedney attempted a 52-yard field goal on the final play of the first half.

Vasher caught the ball deep in the end zone, briefly hesitated, then took off. He reversed field, found a convoy of blockers and raced all the way to the opposite end zone for a 108-yard touchdown.

At the time, it was the longest play in NFL history.

The return gave Chicago a 7-3 halftime lead in a game where points were extremely difficult to find. Adrian Peterson later rushed for a seven-yard touchdown and finished with 120 yards on 24 carries, while Robbie Gould added a fourth-quarter field goal.

The Bears held on for a 17-9 victory, their fifth straight win, improving to 6-3 while maintaining control of the NFC North.

One year later, Devin Hester would return another missed field goal exactly 108 yards against the Giants.

Apparently 108-yard missed field goal returns were just something Bears defensive backs did for a while.

Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs.

#2649. Lazio, Fabiani: “A gennaio non parte nessuno”. Poi sorprende su Floriani

Il ds blinda la rosa per gennaio e, tra i protagonisti della Lazio, indica Floriani: “Ci credevamo, ora sta mostrando chi è”.

Lazio, Fabiani: “A gennaio non parte nessuno”. Poi sorprende su Floriani

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nessuno lascerà la Lazio durante il mercato invernale. A garantirlo è il direttore sportivo biancoceleste Angelo Fabiani, che chiude così la porta a possibili partenze a gennaio nonostante la crescita del valore della rosa.

Il lavoro sul mercato e quello svolto da Gattuso hanno infatti aumentato in maniera esponenziale il valore dei giocatori della Lazio capolista della Serie A. Una situazione che potrebbe inevitabilmente attirare l’attenzione di altri club.

Fabiani, però, non sembra avere alcun dubbio sulle intenzioni della società. E quando gli viene chiesto di scegliere, tra Frattesi, Tavares, Taylor, Belahyane, Noslin e Isaksen, il colpo del quale va maggiormente fiero, il ds sorprende indicando un altro nome: Floriani.

Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, il direttore sportivo della Lazio ha affrontato entrambi gli argomenti nel corso dell’intervista concessa al quotidiano.

La crescita della rosa biancoceleste potrebbe aumentare inevitabilmente l’interesse nei confronti dei calciatori della Lazio. Fabiani riconosce quanto sia aumentato il loro valore, ma esclude possibili “scippi” durante la prossima finestra di mercato.

“Che adesso i giocatori valgano molti di più è un dato di fatto. Ma nel mercato invernale non andrà via nessuno, questo lo posso garantire”.

Parole nette da parte del direttore sportivo. La Lazio, dunque, secondo quanto garantito da Fabiani, non perderà nessuno dei suoi giocatori durante il mercato di gennaio.

A Fabiani vengono poi sottoposti diversi nomi: Frattesi, Tavares, Taylor, Belahyane, Noslin e Isaksen. La domanda è semplice: di quale colpo va più fiero?

Il direttore sportivo parte però da un’esperienza precedente alla Lazio: “Di Napoli, che presi al Messina. Voleva smettere, è diventato Re Artù”.

Quando il discorso si sposta specificamente sulla Lazio, la scelta ricade invece su Floriani.

“Come Lazio dico Floriani. Non è un acquisto, ma un ragazzo che abbiamo cresciuto, mandato a giocare con il premio di valorizzazione perché ci credevamo e ora sta mostrando chi è”.

Una risposta significativa, soprattutto considerando i nomi proposti nella domanda. Fabiani non sceglie uno degli acquisti indicati, ma punta su un giocatore cresciuto dalla Lazio e nel quale, come sottolineato dallo stesso direttore sportivo, il club aveva deciso di credere.

#2648. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2647. Coastal golf course with royal name wraps up renovation in Georgia

The King & Prince Golf and Beach Club on St. Simons Island, Georgia, will reopen for member play Nov. 23 as the completion of the first phase of a multi-year renovation to the coastal property. The golf course was totally reimagined by architect Beau Welling.

The work to the course included rebuilt green complexes, redesigned fairway bunkering, fresh tees, expanded playing options and better sightlines across coastal marshes. Welling focused on enhancing the strategic variety, playability and long-term sustainability of the Lowcountry layout originally designed by Joe Lee, opened in 1989 and now owned by South Street Partners. Welling was able to reduce irrigated turf by 20 percent at the club.

The King & Prince Golf and Beach Club is primarily private but does accept limited guest play from the nearby King & Prince Resort and Club, which also is receiving a renovation that will be complete in May of 2027.

"Working with South Street Partners and the entire King & Prince team on this project has been incredibly rewarding," Welling said in a media release announcing completion of the project. "The property has wonderful natural features, from its live oaks and sandy soils to the marsh views that define this part of the Georgia coast. We wanted to build on those strengths while introducing more strategic variety and creating a course that members will enjoy playing and discovering for years to come."

The work to the club's golf offerings also included a rebuilt driving range, short-game area and practice green. The clubhouse also was updated, as was the restaurant in partnership with chef and restaurateur Ford Fry.

"We're incredibly excited for our members to experience everything that has been thoughtfully planned at The King & Prince Golf Club," Chris Randolph, managing partner at South Street Partners, said in the media release. "From the golf course improvements to the new practice facilities and the renovated clubhouse, this first phase captures our vision to create an exceptional private club in keeping with the character of St. Simons Island while delivering a truly unique member experience."

Jason Lusk is Golfweek's travel and golf course architecture editor, as well as the print magazine's creative director. He has written for and designed Golfweek for more than two decades.

#2646. 5 Bills to pay close attention to vs. the Jets

The Buffalo Bills are Jersey bound, heading to East Rutherford to take on the New York Jets this week. It's just the second divisional game for the Bills, as they have just their October loss vs. the New England Patriots on their AFC East ledger so far. The Jets, meanwhile, will finish their first go-rounds of AFC East games with Sunday's matchup.

While New York may be just 2-7 this season, they've played a lot of tight games, including two against the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins. The Patriots defeated the Jets 26-19, while the Dolphins squeaked out a 28-25 victory. Really, the only game the Jets were entirely demolished in came last week, when they lost 35-12 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Can the Jets play the Bills tight this week? Will Buffalo overlook their division rivals and lose the game outright? There's no question that Buffalo is the better football team, but there's a reason why they play the games rather than just talking about them. The Bills will need to come out ready to roll in order to maintain their hold on the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

Here are five Bills to watch on Sunday as they try to do just that._____________________________________________________________________________

Last week, after a slow start, Allen caught fire in the second half against an outstanding Minnesota Vikings defense. Allen started his night just 7-of-14 for 51 yards and an interception, but from the Bills' two-minute drive at the end of the first half until the end of the game, he was electric. Allen completed 14 of his next 21 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown, and while those numbers might sound pedestrian, Allen finished his day as just the second quarterback to eclipse 200 yards passing against the Vikings this season. It was the first time anyone had done it since Jordan Love did it for the Green Bay Packers in Week One. Allen isn't immune from the occasional stinker, and sometimes, those stinkers come against subpar opponents in the immediate aftermath of a big win. OF Buffalo's three AFC East foes, Allen also has fewer touchdown passes against the Jets (16) than he does against either the Patriots (25) or Dolphins (42) in his career, and he's thrown 11 interceptions in 15 games against them. I want to see Allen work just as patiently as he did on Monday night, taking what the Jets' defense gives him while trusting his teammates to do their part. He doesn't have to play hero ball this week. He just has to be Josh Allen.

Part of me is watching Cook because I expect him to have a big game, as he averaged 4.53 yards per rush in seven career games against the Jets. However, part of me is also watching how head coach and offensive play-caller Joe Brady manages his workload. Cook carried 31 times on Monday, and coming into a short week, I wouldn't be surprised to see more of Ray Davis in the backfield this week. Cook still needs his touches, but I wouldn't be mad if his snap share were dialed back a bit in the interest of saving him for later in the season. Davis and Ty Johnson, who is a former Jet, should see some more work this week. If Cook can slip some big runs early, it could help Buffalo to build the kind of lead where he's hopefully wearing a baseball cap in the fourth quarter.

Yeah, we're going heavy-hitters this week. Moore has looked good since returning from a shoulder injury, but I'm waiting for him to take over a game like he did when he had five catches for 100 yards and a score on opening day. That's also, perhaps not coincidentally, the only game he's played this season where he wasn't banged up in some way. Moore is doing his job, as he has 19 catches fo 285 yards and 2 touchdowns on 32 targets; however, he hasn't looked like a bona fide No. 1 wideout. Against a struggling Jets squad that has allowed 16 passing touchdowns against just one interception this season, I'd like to see Moore have a bigger day. The Jets rank well in passing yards allowed—they're No. 4 in passing yards against—but that's misleading since they're often trailing and they're ranked just 26th against the run. A scoring pass from Allen to Moore on the first drive of the game for the Bills would be a nice way to kick off a Sunday.

Maybe it's unfair to single him out, as Hoecht hasn't played more than 41% of the defensive snaps in a game this season, and he's coming off of Achilles surgery last year. However, he's been mostly pedestrian when he's been out there, and he just hasn't had the burst that he showed in limited action last year. Yes, that's a byproduct of the injury, as he is just past one calendar year since he tore his Achilles in a win over the Chiefs. But, Hoecht has just 15 tackles to show for his work this season, and half a combined sack of Jared Goff in Week Two is his whole pass-rush output so far. He nearly made a cool play last week when he dove and nearly intercepted a spike. Making a play on Geno Smith and bringing the veteran quarterback to the turf would be nice. If Hoecht can find a groove, given how well Greg Rousseau is playing and the strides that T.J. #2643. 3 lessons about Cardinals for Rams to know since Week 6 loss

Former Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur and his Arizona Cardinals pulled off one of the more surprising wins of the season when they beat Sean McVay and company during their Week 6 matchup, 18-16. Since then, the teams have gone in different directions: the Rams have won three straight, while the Cardinals are 1-2, with their one win coming through a wild series of circumstances.

Here are three lessons the Rams have learned about the Cardinals since their first matchup.

Jimmy Garoppolo made the right decision to stay home because the Cardinals' quarterback situation is Baltimore Ravens-level of bad. I would say Baltimore is the worst, but after Arizona benched starter Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew, they traded Brissett to the Ravens.

Minshew suffered an elbow injury last week that landed him on IR, and the Cardinals are set to start rookie quarterback Carson Beck this week. Beck, a collegiate teammate of CJ Daniels, was the starting quarterback of the Miami Hurricanes last season, leading his side to the National Championship Game.

Trey McBride and Michael Wilson on the Arizona Cardinals' offense feels like watching fresh rims get put on a car from 1998. It's not any one person's fault, but a combination of things, including injury issues that have ruled Wilson and WR3 Kendrick Bourne out for the year.

The Cardinals have little depth on offense; they're on their third quarterback with Beck, and it feels like this is the usual part of the year where Arizona starts to fall apart. Long story short, if the Rams scheme Trey McBride out of the offense, they've already won half the battle. The problem is that McBride is very good. The good news is that he's the only major threat the offense has, and LaFleur has a lot of tape for the Rams to learn from.

The only other team to score less than 17 points against the Cardinals this year is the Los Angeles Chargers and their unplugged offense. The Chargers are the 2026 joke of the NFL, as they remain the only winless team in the league, the result of their horrific offense, which is devoid of stars and devastated by injuries and unacceptable play calling.

Regardless of health status, the Rams should be able to bully the Cardinals into a loss as long as they stay ahead of the chains. McVay is too good to be stopped twice in one season, and there's no reason to give Arizona an opening with interceptions and incompletions. Smart, sustained offenses always wither down Arizona by the third quarter. Explosive ones, even when successful, do not tire out their defense. Therefore, the Rams cannot risk a chance of being ineffective, especially without Puka Nacua.

Run the ball, even when they stack the box. It breaks down their whole system.

#2640. Lazio, Piazza della Libertà cambia volto: conclusa la grande riqualificazione

Conclusa la riqualificazione del giardino: nuovi viali, pavimentazione e un'area sportiva nel luogo dove nacque la Lazio.

Lazio, rinasce Piazza della Libertà: nuovo volto per il luogo dove tutto ebbe inizio

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Piazza della Libertà cambia volto e torna a valorizzare uno dei luoghi più significativi della storia della Lazio. Sono terminati gli interventi di riqualificazione e abbellimento del giardino della piazza nella quale, nel 1900, nacque la Società Podistica Lazio.

Oggi, mercoledì 11 novembre, alle ore 13, si è svolto l'incontro tra il Primo Municipio di Roma Capitale e la Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS per presentare i lavori conclusi. Nuovi viali, pavimentazione e un'area attrezzata per lo sport restituiscono un volto rinnovato a uno dei salotti più nobili della Città Eterna.

Una giornata dal significato ancora più profondo per il mondo biancoceleste. Proprio l'11 novembre 2007 moriva Gabriele Sandri, tifoso laziale. Per mantenerne vivo il ricordo, la famiglia ha fortemente voluto la nascita della Fondazione Gabriele Sandri, realtà che proprio da Piazza della Libertà ha dato vita a numerose iniziative sociali e benefiche nel nome di Gabriele.

Secondo quanto riportato dalla Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS, la conclusione degli interventi rappresenta un nuovo passo nel percorso di valorizzazione di un luogo indissolubilmente legato alla storia biancoceleste.

È proprio da Piazza della Libertà che ebbe inizio un'avventura lunga ormai oltre 126 anni. Una storia che nel tempo ha attraversato campi di gioco, piscine, fiumi e laghi, parquet dei palazzetti, piste degli stadi, cieli e montagne. Ovunque fosse possibile praticare sport, lì è arrivata la Lazio.

I lavori sono stati realizzati attraverso risorse PNRR, nell'ambito del progetto Caput Mundi, gestito dal Ministero del Turismo e la cui attuazione è stata affidata alla Struttura commissariale per il Giubileo 2025. Gli interventi hanno interessato diverse zone del giardino con l'obiettivo di aumentarne fruibilità, accessibilità e qualità urbana.

Sono stati costruiti tre nuovi viali. Il primo collega via Cesi con l'interno del giardino. Il secondo attraversa la zona centrale dell'area in direzione del viale interno già esistente, mentre il terzo conduce verso la Torretta della Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS.

È stata inoltre realizzata la pavimentazione dello spazio che circonda la Torretta lungo i tre lati rivolti verso il giardino. Nell'area centrale sono state posizionate anche due lastre di travertino, utilizzate per la copertura e il livellamento dello spazio.

Particolare attenzione è stata riservata allo sport. Sul lato del giardino rivolto verso Ponte Regina Margherita è nata una nuova area attrezzata. Sono state installate una struttura calistenica con barre per le trazioni e panca, collocata su una pavimentazione antitrauma, oltre a una struttura bikefit.

All'incontro hanno preso parte l'assessore municipale Stefano Marin e i rappresentanti della Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS.

Grande soddisfazione è stata espressa da Marco Chiarion Casoni, presidente della Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS.

«Siamo orgogliosi e felici che Piazza della Libertà, sede della nascita e parte fondamentale della storia della nostra Società, sia stata interessata da un intervento così importante – dichiara Casoni –. La riqualificazione, il rinnovamento degli spazi e la presenza di nuove attrezzature sportive restituiscono alla piazza una maggiore qualità e una nuova capacità di essere vissuta dalla cittadinanza».

Il percorso, tuttavia, non si fermerà con la conclusione di questi lavori.

«Ma il progetto di valorizzazione non finisce qui – aggiunge Casoni –. Insieme al Primo Municipio stiamo lavorando per continuare ad abbellire e valorizzare Piazza della Libertà. Per noi è particolarmente significativo poter contribuire alla cura di un luogo nel quale, 126 anni fa, è iniziata la storia della Lazio. Ringraziamo le istituzioni e l'architetto Romolo Crescenzi per il lavoro svolto e per aver reso possibile questa evoluzione».

Soddisfazione anche da parte del Municipio Roma I Centro. L'assessore Stefano Marin ha sottolineato il valore dell'intervento per la città e per il territorio.

«Ringrazio la Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS per la collaborazione e tutti coloro che hanno contribuito alla realizzazione di questi interventi. Piazza della Libertà è un luogo importante per la storia sportiva e per la vita del nostro territorio. Siamo felici di restituire ai cittadini uno spazio più bello, accessibile e vivibile», dichiara Marin.

Una Piazza della Libertà rinnovata, dunque, ma sempre profondamente legata alle proprie radici. Proprio lì dove, 126 anni fa, iniziò la storia della Lazio.

#2639. How’s the weather looking in South Bend for Boston College-Notre Dame?

US LBM Coaches Poll No. 3 Notre Dame is set to face Boston College for the 29th time on Saturday afternoon.

While it's an exciting time to be a Fighting Irish fan as they battle the Eagles for the Ireland Trophy in the latest edition of the "Holy War," the weather might not be ideal for the teams and the spectators at Notre Dame Stadium.

"It's not exactly the most pleasant day to play football, but hey, it is November in South Bend," ABC57 News meteorologist Dave Caulfield said in his weather report on Friday.

According to The Weather Channel, the temperature in South Bend could be in the low 40s between tailgating, the 3:30 p.m. kickoff and by the conclusion of the game around 7 p.m. ET.

There is a 37% chance of showers at 3 p.m., but the forecast is projected as cloudy heading into the evening.

"Some rain/snow showers are possible for tailgating, but drizzle could linger into the start of the game," Caulfield posted on social media. "Despite the forecast, I still don't believe the weather will have a big impact for Notre Dame and Boston College."

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2635. Group of retired MLB umpires, including Joe West, file lawsuit alleging they are owed more than $2 million

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former MLB umpire Joe West is part of a group of five retired umpires who are suing their pension plan and alleging they have been underpaid by the plan, the Associated Press reports. West, along with Tom Hallion, Gerry Davis, Larry Vanover, and Jerry Layne, filed the suit in late September in federal court in New York.

The suit alleges that the five umpires have been underpaid by the pension plan by more than $2 million. According to the AP, the suit "was filed against the American Leagues and National Leagues of Professional Baseball Clubs Retirement Income Plan for Umpires and that entity's retirement committee." The five umpires claim their benefits were not calculated correctly and therefore should receive additional money.

West, 74, retired from umpiring in MLB in 2021 after umpiring more than 5,000 games at the highest level starting in 1976. The man they called "Cowboy Joe" umpired a record 5,460 games in all, was known as a colorful figure in the sport and sometimes even a source of controversy.

In 2021, West won more than $500,000 in damages as the result of a defamation suit against former MLB player Paul Lo Duca after Lo Duca alleged during a podcast that West would "open up the strike zone" for reliever Billy Wagner in exchange for driving one of Wagner's vintage cars.

West referenced his "history with lawsuits" on Thursday. From the AP:

West said that when he brought up the issue to the retirement committee, he was offered a relatively small sum. West said MLB senior vice president and chief employment counsel Steven Gonzalez told him: "If you don't like the number, sue us."

"Does Steve Gonzalez not know my history with dealing with lawsuits?" West said.

Like West, Davis also retired after the 2021 season while Hallion umpired through the 2022 season and Layne and Vanover stepped away after the 2024 campaign. The five sued as individuals and did not involve the umpires' union, their lawyer, Paul B. Holmes, said, per the AP.

A pretrial conference in the case is scheduled for Dec. 11.

#2633. Ex-Guardians catcher Bo Naylor testifies in defense of Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz in MLB pitch-rigging trial

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former Cleveland Guardians catcher Bo Naylor on Thursday testified in federal court that he perceived nothing untoward about disputed pitches thrown by former All-Star closer Emmanuel Clase and his former Guardians teammate Luis Ortiz, ESPN reports.

Naylor, who played five seasons for the Guardians, appeared as a witness for the defense in the ongoing federal trial in which prosecutors allege that Clase and Ortiz rigged multiple pitches for the benefit of co-conspiring bettors. In Clase's case, he's alleged to have done so in 17 games across a two-year period beginning in May 2023. Naylor, now a member of the Milwaukee Brewers, was catcher for some of Clase's disputed appearances during that span, including seven of the 18 pitches he's alleged to have rigged.

Naylor, a defense witness, was shown video replays of some of the pitches the government alleges were predetermined by Clase or Ortiz as part of the scheme. Naylor was behind the plate for many of them and said they looked like common sliders outside the strike zone. He said the scouting reports on the hitters Ortiz faced during the two pitches in question indicated that sliders low and away would be a "weapon."

In November 2025, Clase and Ortiz were indicted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. According to the Department of Justice, both pitchers "agreed in advance with their co-conspirators to throw specific types of pitches and speeds of pitches." The Department of Justice alleged that the pair made at least $450,000 by rigging outings and throwing specific pitches to benefit bettors who wagered on the outcomes of those pitches.

Both Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to those charges in November of last year. Clase and Ortiz have been on administrative leave since late June 2025 while Major League Baseball investigates. MLB has the authority to discipline the pitchers regardless of how the criminal trial plays out.

The pair could face up to 65 years in prison if convicted on the charges of wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery, and money laundering conspiracy.

Il dj romano viaggiava con alcuni amici verso Milano per assistere a Inter-Lazio quando fu colpito durante una sosta.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Un agente della Polizia Stradale esplose alcuni colpi di pistola. Uno raggiunse Sandri mentre si trovava all’interno di un’automobile.

#2628. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2625. Five under-the-radar MLB free agents who could make a big impact next season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is a little more than a week old now and we're still waiting for the first big trade or free agent signing. That isn't unusual, though. The hot stove, like the regular season, is a marathon, not a sprint. A lockout is expected when the collective bargaining agreement ends at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and there should be a flurry of activity before then.

We ranked the offseason's top 50 free agents, and although it is not a great class, there are dozens of quality players available. You just have to know where to look. Here now are five players who did not rank among our top 50 free agents, but would nonetheless be good options and solid pickups for teams that want to raise their floor and improve their supporting cast.

It was a tale of two seasons for the 29-year-old Bryan Abreu, who had a 5.81 ERA before the All-Star break and a 1.71 ERA after. The under-the-hood estimators, like FIP and xERA, were better in the second half as well, though Abreu lost close to 2 mph off his fastball this year and, not coincidentally, a whole bunch of swings and misses. Abreu is third in appearances and second in innings among relievers since 2022 and it's possible the workload is catching up to him. There's still enough bat-missing ability and late-inning experience here for Abreu to contribute to a contender's bullpen. It just might happen as a seventh-inning guy moving forward, not as the Moment of Truth™ reliever who pitches in the game's biggest moments.

If you're looking for a bottom of the order guy who will take walks and give you 10-15 home runs, that's J.P. Crawford. His defense, specifically his range and arm, has slipped so much in his early 30s that he's no longer a viable shortstop, though he played 33 games at third base this past season. I like him better at second base, but third base works too. Crawford gets on-base at a decent clip and won't strike out excessively, plus he's long been regarded as an excellent teammate and grade-A clubhouse guy. It seems like his time with the Mariners is over and it's for the best. Crawford can go elsewhere, play a new position, and just be part of the lineup rather than one of the faces of the franchise.

Due to injury and ineffectiveness, it looked like Sean Newcomb was on his way out of baseball two years ago. He then reinvented himself as a sinker/curveball guy and carved out a nice second phase to his career as a workhorse utility reliever who won't beat himself with walks (an early career bugaboo) and will limit hard contact in the air. Newcomb, 33, worked at least 90 innings the last two seasons while pitching in every possible role. He closed out games, worked high leverage as a setup guy, soaked up innings in long relief, and opened a few times as well. Newcomb is likely miscast as a go-to bullpen option, though he can be a valuable third or fourth option for a contender. The utility reliever is all the rage these days and Newcomb fits the profile to a T.

Now 35, Emilio Pagán was sensational after returning from a hamstring injury in July, pitching to a 1.88 ERA with 34 strikeouts and only five walks in his final 28 ⅔ innings. The downside is the same as it's always been: Pagán is exceptionally home run prone (career 1.51 HR/9), which is a bad trait for a late-inning reliever who pitches almost exclusively in close games. His fastball remains firm, though, and his splitter is an elite swing-and-miss pitch that allows him to neutralize righties and lefties. As long as you're willing to live with the home run risk, Pagán remains a capable high-leverage reliever, one who is not out of place pitching important innings for a contending team.

Platoon DHs are not the hottest commodity, but Joc Pederson fills the role about as well as anyone in the game. He's a left-handed hitter, so he's on the heavy side of the platoon, and he authored a .245/.338/.496 line with terrific ball-tracking data (exit velocity, etc.) against righties. If you must play him in the field, Pederson can stand in right field or at first base for about six innings before being subbed out for a defensive replacement. He's essentially a bat-only player, though. Pederson will turn 35 in April and he's still a powerful and productive hitter against righties and an elite clubhouse vibes dude.

Future Hall of Famer Max Scherzer will pitch in "lockout games" this offseason to determine whether he will continue his career, reports the New York Post. Multiple teams have interest in free agent Ty France, according to The Athletic. A deal could come together quickly. It's unclear which teams are in the hunt for France, though there is no shortage of contenders who could use the 32-year-old. #2620. MLB free agency: Six international players to know for the 2026-27 offseason

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Major League Baseball's free agency period opened earlier this week and teams are now clear to pursue any roster upgrades they deem necessary. That includes players coming over from Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball league, South Korea's Korea Baseball Organization, and Taiwan's Chinese Professional Baseball League. Those are high-level leagues that have sent many impact players MLB's way over the years.

Look no farther than the Dodgers to see how important international talent can be to a club. The Dodgers employed four different former NPB and KBO players this past season, including two-way star Shohei Ohtani, ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and starter Roki Sasaki. Ohtani was signed as an MLB free agent, but the others went to the Dodgers through the posting system.

Per the posting agreement with MLB, posted NPB and CPBL players get a 45-day window to negotiate and sign with an MLB team. KBO players get a 30-day window. Players who do not sign during that posting window return to their previous team in NPB, CPBL, or KBO. The MLB team that signs a posted player pays a fee to the player's former NPB, CPBL, or KBO team.

$5M plus 17.5% of contract value over $25M

$9.375M plus 15% of contract value over $50M

For example, the White Sox paid Munetaka Murakami's former team, the Yakult Swallows, a $6.575 million posting fee on his $34 million contract last offseason. That's $5 million on the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the remaining $9 million, which is $1.575 million. The $5 million plus $1.575 million equals the $6.575 million posting fee paid to the Swallows.

Unlike last lockout, MLB will not be pausing the signing window during the expected lockout, according to The Athletic. In other words, if owners lock players out on Dec. 1 as expected, that date will essentially serve as the same deadline for already posted NPB players unless the lockout ends before their 45-day window expires.

There are no superstar-caliber players like Ohtani or Yamamoto available in this winter's international free agent crop. There are, however, several interesting players who can improve an MLB roster in 2027. Here are the six best NPB, CPBL, and KBO players to know this offseason.

Japan's Triple Crown winner hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. He has a similar skill set to Murakami but is not exactly Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games in 2026 around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll. The Hanshin Tigers officially posted Sato on Nov. 1.

Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Taira was officially posted on Nov. 1.

A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters posted Itoh on Nov. 1.

Roh has an unusual agreement with the Hanwha Eagles. He signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and roughly $23 million), and as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him for MLB teams this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the Eagles to finish his career when his big-league stint is over. This past season, Roh, 26 in November, authored a .283/.360/.505 batting line with 29 home runs. He has real right-handed power and a good approach at the plate. There are concerns about his propensity to swing and miss as well as his arm at the hot corner. The Eagles formally posted Roh on Nov. 1.

The Seibu Lions posted Takahashi last offseason, but he was unable to find a contract to his liking, so he returned to Japan for another season and threw 148 innings with a 2.64 ERA. Takahashi, 30 in February, is an international free agent now, meaning he does not have to be posted and can instead negotiate at his own pace. More of a ground ball pitcher than a bat-misser, Takahashi sits in the 91-95 mph range with his fastball and has two good secondary pitches in his slider and splitter. He also throws a cutter and curveball. Takahashi is considered a potential innings guy for the back of an MLB rotation.

Tseng pitched for Chinese Taipei in the World Baseball Classic in 2023 and 2026 and he has been one of the CPBL's top relievers the last few years. In 2026, he saved 25 games with a 1.80 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 52 ⅓ innings. Tseng's fastball typically sits in the mid-90s and has run as high as 100 mph in the past, though it has been a few years. His go-to secondary pitch is a breaking ball that needs improvement for Tseng to carve out an MLB career as more than a middle reliever.

#2616. MLB rumors: Why the Dodgers could be Tarik Skubal or bust; Red Sox looking for pitching depth

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The biggest thing hanging over baseball this offseason is obviously the expiration of the CBA and what everyone assumes will be a lockout. Until then, we'll find out the major award winners this coming week, starting with Rookies of the Year on Monday. And, of course, there's the player movement yet to come.

For the latter, let's round up Sunday's rumors right here.

As we saw plenty in 2026, the Dodgers have a very talented rotation with a few injury-prone parts (Tyler Glasnow, Blake Snell, Shohei Ohtani as a pitcher, etc.). As such, this bit of speculative reporting from The Athletic makes a ton of sense:

The Dodgers will need someone who can cover innings in 2027. It's just a matter of how much they can lean on Justin Wrobleski, trust how Emmet Sheehan finished the season (I'd say probably a good amount), how healthy Gavin Stone is (unknown), how ready Jackson Ferris is (he seems close) and if they have enough depth options behind them.

All that to say, the Dodgers will be in on Skubal. If he goes elsewhere, I don't think it's as simple as the Dodgers going after the next highest-ranked starter on the market, such as a Freddy Peralta or a Michael King. I could see them taking a flier on some depth options to soak up innings in anticipation of a quick ramp-up post-lockout, sort of like they did when they signed Tyler Anderson in the run-up to the 2022 season.

Yes, the Dodgers are in on the Tarik Skubal bidding. We all know that. But if they lose out on retaining the two-time Cy Young winner, they may not just continue moving down the list for available starters. Then again, it's hard to ever know exactly what Andrew Friedman is going to spend money on.

As things stand, the Dodgers' rotation has Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Snell, Glasnow, Roki Sasaki and Sheehan, at least until Ohtani is ready to rejoin the fray.

Coming off two straight Wild Card Series losses and sub-90-win seasons, the Red Sox would surely like to take things up a notch for the 2027 season. One way might be to build out the depth of the pitching staff. They'll be "in the market for a back-end starter" and a right-handed reliever "with swing-and-miss capability," according to MassLive.

For the rotation: Sonny Gray hits free agency, but Garrett Crochet will return from a nearly full-season injury. Payton Tolle and Ranger Suárez fill the 2-3 spots, with Jake Bennett solid as the No. 4. That leaves Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford and Tanner Houck as options for the fifth spot in addition to depth. It doesn't seem dire, but we've seen plenty of times what kind of havoc injuries can wreak.

In the bullpen, lefty Aroldis Chapman returns at closer with Garrett Whitlock and Erik Miller as setup men. Houck missing out on a rotation spot could mean he helps late as well.

#2613. MLB rumors: Why the Cubs may already be out on Tarik Skubal, plus latest on Phillies, Cardinals, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22.

Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are already flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Monday's supply just below.

The expectation remains that we'll see some level of activity on the trade and free agency fronts before the lockout begins in early December. As noted above, that was indeed the case leading up to the last lockout, and this time around, the prospect of drastic changes in the next CBA may have big-spending teams looking to fortify their rosters before those changes are implemented. Speaking of which, MLB Network reports that we could see some notable transactions go down at the upcoming General Managers Meetings, which take place from Nov. 10-12 in Las Vegas.

During a standard offseason, not much beyond behind-the-scenes groundwork goes down during the GM Meetings, and the real moves start happening at the December Winter Meetings. However, unless the lockout is resolved quickly – highly unlikely – then there probably won't be a Winter Meetings this offseason. That means the GM Meetings could be more active than usual.

Free agent ace and, until later this week, reigning back-to-back  American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal is the prize of the offseason. The 29-year-old lefty is a fit for any of MLB's 30 teams, but heretofore the most serious bidders have been expected to be the Los Angeles Dodgers (who acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers leading up to last season's trade deadline), the New York Mets, and the Chicago Cubs. Now, though, perhaps you can reduce that number of serious bidders to two. While Chicago very much needs rotation help for 2027 and beyond, the Athletic reports that the Cubs "are expected to stay on the sidelines" when the Skubal bidding gets serious. That, no doubt, will come as a disappointment to Cubs fans who are still waiting for the Ricketts to invest in the payroll at levels befitting a big-market contender.

The Cardinals traded away veteran lefty reliever JoJo Romero, along with starter and fellow free agent Dustin May, to the Milwaukee Brewers leading up to the trade deadline. Now, St. Louis may be interested in bringing Romero back on a free agent contract, the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports.

Romero, 30, is coming off a 2026 season in which he pitched to a 3.36 ERA with a 3.00 K/BB ratio in 55 appearances. In the postseason with Milwaukee, Romero had a 1.13 ERA with 11 strikeouts and one walk in eight innings. He previously spent parts of five seasons with the Cardinals.

Do the Philadelphia Phillies need a new shortstop? That's one of the principal questions of their offseason. Although incumbent Trea Turner is signed through 2033, his defense at the crucial position of shortstop has degraded into "unplayable" territory, and that has the Phils considering fallback options should Turner need to be moved off the position. One option is free agent 31-year-old Ha-Seong Kim, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports. Kim, 32, spent last season on a one-year deal with the division-rival Atlanta Braves. He's been a primary shortstop for five of his six MLB seasons, and while he's certainly not among the very best at the position, he does profile as a major defensive upgrade over Turner. As for the bat, Kim for his career has an OPS+ of 93, and he's capable of stealing a base on occasion. He was, however, an offensive sinkhole for 51 games in 2026. Turner, meantime, may be looking at a switch to the outfield starting next season as the Phillies attempt to keep their contending window open.

#2612. Dodgers notes: Pedro Guerrero, Shohei Ohtani, Yoshinobu Yamamoto

We've had a relatively busy last few days, with Shohei Ohtani finishing second in National League MVP voting and climbing up the all-time award share leaderboard, Yoshinobu Yamamoto voted fourth place for the NL Cy Young Award, and old friend Evan Phillips joining the Atlanta Braves bullpen for three years, $35 million, outpacing several contract projections.

The Dodgers this week also hired Pedro Guerrero as a hitting coach, replacing the departing Aaron Bates on the major league staff. Guerrero has coached the last nine years in the majors, and before that was a minor league player and coach in the Dodgers system.

Fabian Ardaya at The Athletic talked to Guerrero and others about the new hire, including Miami Marlins manager Clayton McCullough, the Dodgers former first base coach and previous minor league coordinator:

"(He can) meet guys where they are," McCullough said. "He is a good listener. That's where he really does his best work. Some of those conversations, either in the cage during the day, with just trying to have a guy be in the best spot mentally that he can be for that given day. Then in the game, not letting some of the anxiety or some of the stress (pile up) for a player, he helps alleviate a lot of that."

Sam Miller at his Pebble Hunting newsletter wrote about various ways the Dodgers have been beatable, and along the way detailed the various ways baseball is essentially impossible to guarantee a particular outcome.

What has become an annual treat is Davy Andrews at FanGraphs perusing various baseball news items to chronicle various instances of teams saying essentially "we tried" as a way to placate an unfulfilled acquisition. This offseason's first such instance appeared to come this week.
